#DantePH Update (as of 5 p.m., 22 July 2025)
The low pressure area east of Aurora developed into tropical depression Dante.
Dante is not seen to make landfall but will enhance the southwest monsoon or habagat through Friday, July 25.
No wind signals are expected to be hoisted.
The enhanced habagat will bring significant rainfall over Luzon and some parts of Visayas.
Up to torrential rains may be expected over Pangasinan, Zambales, Bataan, Cavite, Batangas, Occidental Mindoro, and Metro Manila.
Serious threats of flooding and landslides remain.
Dante was spotted 1,130 km east of Northern Luzon at 4 p.m. Tuesday, with winds of 45 kph and gusts up to 55 kph. It is moving north northwestward at 20 kph.
The disturbance will intensify up to tropical storm strength while moving northwestward over the Philippine Sea.
It may exit the Philippine area of responsibility late Thursday or early Friday.
Meanwhile, the low pressure area near Batanes may either merge with the broader circulation of Dante or cross Extreme Northern Luzon towards the northern West Philippine Sea. #WeatherPatrol | via Ariel Rojas, ABS-CBN News

TROPICAL CYCLONE BULLETIN NR. 1
Tropical Depression #DantePH
Issued at 5:00 PM, 22 July 2025
Valid for broadcast until the next bulletin at 11:00 PM today.
THE LOW PRESSURE AREA EAST OF AURORA DEVELOPED INTO TROPICAL DEPRESSION “DANTE”
• Location of Center (4:00 PM):
The center of Tropical Depression DANTE was estimated based on all available data at 1,115 km East Northeast of Central Luzon or 1,130 km East of Northern Luzon (18.3°N, 132.4°E).
• Intensity:
Maximum su stained winds of 45 km/h near the center, gustiness of up to 55 km/h, and central pressure of 1000 hPa
• Present Movement:
North northwestward at 20 km/h
• Extent of Tropical Cyclone Winds:
Strong winds extend outwards up to 220 km from the center
TROPICAL CYCLONE WIND SIGNALS (TCWS) IN EFFECT
• No Wind Signal currently hoisted.
OTHER HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND AREAS
• Heavy Rainfall Outlook
Refer to Weather Advisory No. 29 issued at 5:00 PM today for the heavy rainfall outlook due to the Southwest Monsoon enhanced by DANTE, the Low Pressure Area east of Batanes, and Tropical Cyclone WIPHA over Vietnam
• Severe Winds
The enhanced Southwest Monsoon will bring strong to gale-force gusts over the following areas (especially in coastal and upland areas exposed to winds):
• Today: Zambales, Bataan, Metro Manila, CALABARZON, MIMAROPA, Visayas, and Dinagat Islands
• Tomorrow (23 July): Ilocos Region, Zambales, Bataan, Bulacan, Metro Manila, CALABARZON, MIMAROPA, Visayas, Zamboanga del Norte, Misamis Occidental, Lanao del Norte, Camiguin, and Dinagat Islands.
• Friday (18 July): Ilocos Region, Abra, Benguet, Central Luzon, Metro Manila, CALABARZON, MIMAROPA, Visayas, Zamboanga del Norte, Misamis Occidental, Lanao del Norte Camiguin, and Dinagat Islands.
HAZARDS AFFECTING COASTAL WATERS
• 24-Hour Sea Condition Outlook
Up to rough seas over the following coastal waters:
• Up to 3.0 m: The seaboards of Batanes and Kalayaan Islands; the western seaboards of Zambales, Bataan, Lubang Island, Occidental Mindoro, and Calamian Islands.
• Mariners of small seacrafts, including all types of motorbancas, are advised not to venture out to sea under these conditions, especially if inexperienced or operating ill-equipped vessels.
Up to moderate seas over the following coastal waters:
• Up to 2.5 m: The seaboards of Babuyan Island and Ilocos Region; the southern seaboard of Bataan; the western seaboards of Cavite, Batangas, and Palawan.
• Up to 2.0 m: The seaboards of Camarines Norte, Oriental Mindoro, Marinduque, and Romblon; the northern and eastern seaboards of Catanduanes and Northern Samar; the eastern seaboards of Albay, Sorsogon and Davao Oriental; the western seaboard of Masbate; the southern seaboard of Quezon; the  remaining seaboard of Batangas and Occidental Mindoro; the northern seaboard of Camarines Sur.
• Mariners of motorbancas and similarly-sized vessels are advised to take precautionary measures while venturing out to sea and, if possible, avoid navigation under these conditions.
TRACK AND INTENSITY OUTLOOK
• DANTE is forecast to move northward or north northwestward over the Philippine Sea from tonight to tomorrow (23 July), before turning northwestward towards the Ryukyu Islands and the East China Sea. On the track forecast, DANTE may exit the Philippine Area of Responsibility (PAR) on Thursday (24 July) or on Friday (25 July).
• DANTE may reach tropical storm category tomorrow. Further intensification into a severe tropical storm remains less likely but is not ruled out.
Considering these developments, the public and disaster risk reduction and management offices concerned are advised to take all necessary measures to protect life and property. Persons living in areas identified to be highly or very highly susceptible to these hazards are advised to follow evacuation and other instructions from local officials. For heavy rainfall warnings, thunderstorm/rainfall advisories, and other severe weather information specific to your area, please monitor products issued by your local PAGASA Regional Services Division.
The next tropical cyclone bulletin will be issued at 11:00 PM today.
DOST-PAGASA

Aside from the regular clearing operations, MMDA rescue personnel are also on standby along with the agency’s assets to provide immediate response.

The Department of Science and Technology (DOST) conducted the 8th National Research and Development Conference (NRDC) participated by government funding agencies, local government units, academe, and research and development institutes on July 23-24, 2025 at The Manila Hotel, City of Manila.
On the first day, DOST-PHIVOLCS and DOST-PAGASA facilitated the breakout session on Wealth Protection, one of the four pillars of DOST that intensifies the development and transfer of more climate and disaster-resilient technologies and provides science and technology-based information and services for warning, disaster preparedness, and mitigation.
Ms. Charmaine V. Villamil, DOST-PHIVOLCS Senior Science Research Specialist (SRS), provided the preliminaries and moderated the session. DOST-PHIVOLCS Director Teresito C. Bacolcol delivered the opening remarks and session overview.
Ms. Mabelline T. Cahulogan, Supervising SRS of DOST-PHIVOLCS, presented a topic on “Enhancing Disaster Resilience and Climate Adaptation: The Critical Role of Geospatial Technology in Safeguarding National Wealth in the Philippines.” Ms. Joan C. Salcedo, Supervising SRS of DOST-PHIVOLCS, imparted her insights on “Empowering Decision-Makers through REDAS: A Multi-Hazard Simulation and Impact Assessment Tool.” 
Other speakers were Secretary Robert E.A. Borje, Vice Chairperson and Executive Director of the Climate Change Commission; Mr. Emmanuel T. Balajadia of the Office of Civil Defense; and Dr. Marcelino Q. Villafuerte II, Deputy Administrator for Research and Development of DOST-PAGASA. Dr. Joseph Q. Basconcillo, Scientist I and Senior Weather Specialist of DOST-PAGASA, led the open forum and synthesis. The session ended with a closing remarks from Dr. Nathaniel T. Servando, DOST-PAGASA Administrator. 
In addition, DOST-PHIVOLCS showcased its DOST-funded "Accelerated Earthquake Multi-hazards Mapping and Risk Assessment Program of the Philippines" (ACER) Program in the exhibit hall.
With this year’s theme, “R&D Building Lives: Leveraging Transdisciplinary R&D for Well-being, Wealth Creation, Wealth Protection, and Sustainability,” the NRDC aims to promote multi-disciplinary and collaborative R&D, to coordinate and rationalize the R&D agenda, to harmonize all R&D agenda and priorities, and to facilitate dissemination of outputs of programs and projects under the Harmonized National R&D Agenda to various research institutions and agencies.

Issued at 5:00 PM, 24 July 2025
“DANTE” HAS EXITED THE PHILIPPINE AREA OF RESPONSIBILITY.
• Location of Center (10:00 AM)
The center of Tropical Storm DANTE was estimated based on all available data at 805 km Northeast of Extreme Northern Luzon (25.3°N, 128.0°E) (OUTSIDE PAR). 
• Intensity 
Maximum sustained winds of 75 km/h near the center, gustiness of up to 90 km/h, and central pressure of 994 hPa. 
• Present Movement 
Northward at 15 km/h 
• Extent of Tropical Cyclone Winds 
Strong to gale-force winds extend outwards up to 550 km from the center 
TROPICAL CYCLONE WIND SIGNALS (TCWS) IN EFFECT
• No Wind Signal currently hoisted.
OTHER HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND AREAS
• Heavy Rainfall Outlook
Refer to Weather Advisory No. 37 issued at 5:00 PM today for the heavy rainfall outlook due to EMONG and the Southwest Monsoon enhanced by DANTE and EMONG.
• Severe Winds
The enhanced Southwest Monsoon will bring strong to gale-force gusts over the following areas (especially in coastal and upland areas exposed to winds):
• Today: Central Luzon (areas not under Wind Signal), Metro Manila, CALABARZON, Bicol Region, MIMAROPA, Visayas, Zamboanga del Norte, Misamis Occidental, Lanao del Norte, Camiguin, Dinagat Islands, and Davao Oriental.
• Tomorrow (25 July): Central Luzon (areas not under Wind Signal), Metro Manila, CALABARZON, Bicol Region, MIMAROPA, Visayas, Zamboanga del Norte, Misamis Occidental, Lanao del Norte, and Camiguin.
• Saturday (26 July): Batanes, Babuyan Islands, Ilocos Region, Isabela, Quirino, Nueva Vizcaya, Central Luzon, Metro Manila, Bicol Region, MIMAROPA, Visayas, Zamboanga del Norte, Misamis Occidental, Lanao del Norte, and Camiguin.
HAZARDS AFFECTING COASTAL WATERS
A Gale Warning is in effect over the seaboard of Northern Luzon and the western seaboards of Central and Southern Luzon. Refer to Gale Warning No. 4 issued at 5:00 PM today.
• 24-Hour Sea Condition Outlook
Forecast wave heights are not related to storm surge heights.
Up to very rough or high seas over the following coastal waters:
• Up to 14.0 m: The western seaboards of Ilocos Sur, La Union, and Pangasinan.
• Up to 8.0 m: The western seaboard of Zambales; the remaining seaboard of Pangasinan.
• Up to 6.0 m: The western seaboard of Bataan.
• Up to 4.5 m: The western seaboards of Batangas, Lubang Islands, and Occidental Mindoro.
• Sea travel is risky all types or tonnage of vessels. All mariners must remain in port or, if underway, seek shelter or safe harbor as soon as possible until winds and waves subside. 
Up to rough seas over the following coastal waters:
• Up to 4.0 m: The eastern seaboards of Isabela and mainland Cagayan.
• Up to 3.5 m: The western seaboards of northern Palawan including Calamian Islands; the northeastern seaboard of Aurora.
• Up to 3.0 m: The seaboards of Batanes, Marinduque, and Kalayaan Islands; the seaboards of Babuyan Islands; the southern seaboard of Quezon; the eastern seaboard of Oriental Mindoro; the northern and western seaboards of Romblon; the remaining seaboards of Bataan
• Mariners of small seacrafts, including all types of motorbancas, are advised not to venture out to sea under these conditions, especially if inexperienced or operating ill-equipped vessels.

• Up to 2.5 m: The remaining seaboards of mainland Cagayan, Aurora, and Cavite; the seaboards of Pampanga, Bulacan, Metro Manila, and Surigao del Sur; the western seaboards of southern Palawan and Antique; the eastern seaboard of Catanduanes and Davao Oriental
• Up to 2.0 m: The seaboards of Aklan, and Northern Samar; the remaining seaboards of Bicol Region, Batangas, Quezon,  Occidental Mindoro, Oriental Mindoro, Palawan, and Romblon; the southwestern seaboard of Negros Occidental and Iloilo; the western seaboard of Guimaras.  
• Mariners of motorbancas and similarly-sized vessels are advised to take precautionary measures while venturing out to sea and, if possible, avoid navigation under these conditions.
TRACK AND INTENSITY OUTLOOK
• DANTE is now outside the Philippine Area of Responsibility. On the forecast track, this tropical storm will move west northwestward towards the Ryukyu Islands. Tomorrow (25 July) until the end of the forecast period, It will continue to move westward over the East China Sea. 
• DANTE is forecast to weaken for the remainder of the forecast period until it becomes a remnant low on Saturday (26 July).

ATM: REDAS Training Reaches Sorsogon Province
DOST-PHIVOLCS leads a training on "Mainstreaming Disaster Risk Reduction into the Local Development, Contingency, and Emergency Preparedness Planning Process through the Use of REDAS Software" for Sorsogon Province. 
The training, held at Cristina’s Resort and Hotel, Sorsogon City on July 21-25, 2025, features three modules including REDAS function to simulate earthquake hazards, such as ground shaking, liquefaction, landslides, and tsunami.
Mr. Raden D. Dimaano, Head of the Provincial Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office (PDRRMO), welcomed the participants while Mr. Franco Eric O. Ravanilla, Sorsogon Provincial Administrator, sent his message of support to this initiative.
Training participants represent the PDRRMO, Provincial Planning and Development Office, and Provincial Agriculturist Office, and Municipalities of Barcelona, Bulan, Bulusan, Castilla, Casiguran, Donsol, Gubat, Irosin, Juban, Magallanes, Pilar, Prieto Diaz, and Sorsogon City. Also, personnel from Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG) Sorsogon, Philippine National Police, and guest participants from Hinundayan and Malitbog in Southern Leyte and Bacacay in Albay joined the training.

TROPICAL CYCLONE BULLETIN NR. 10
Typhoon #EmongPH (CO-MAY)
Issued at 8:00 PM, 24 July 2025
Valid for broadcast until the next bulletin at 11:00 PM today.
TYPHOON “EMONG” MAINTAINS ITS STRENGTH AND IS NEARING LANDFALL OVER WESTERN PANGASINAN
• Location of Center (7:00 PM):
The center of the eye of Typhoon EMONG was estimated based on all available data including from Subic Doppler Weather Radar over the coastal waters of Burgos, Pangasinan (16.0°N, 119.3°E). 
• Intensity 
Maximum sustained winds of 120 km/h near the center, gustiness of up to 165 km/h, and central pressure of 975 hPa.
• Present Movement:
Eastward slowly 
• Extent of Tropical Cyclone Winds:
Strong to typhoon-force winds extend outwards up to 240 km from the center 
TROPICAL CYCLONE WIND SIGNALS (TCWS) IN EFFECT
TCWS No.4
 • Wind threat: Typhoon-force winds
 • Warning lead time: 12 hours
 • Range of wind speeds: 118 to 184 km/h (Beaufort 12)
 • Potential impacts of winds: Significant to severe threat to life and property
LUZON:
The southwestern portion of Ilocos Sur (Santa Lucia, Santa Cruz, Tagudin), the northwestern portion of La Union (Bangar, Luna, Balaoan, Bacnotan, San Juan, City of San Fernando, Bauang), and the extreme northwestern portion of Pangasinan (Agno, Bani, Bolinao, Anda, City of Alaminos)

LUZON:
The rest of Ilocos Norte, the rest of Pangasinan, Apayao, Kalinga, the rest of Mountain Province, Ifugao, the rest of Benguet, Babuyan Islands, the northern and western portions of mainland Cagayan (Rizal, Santa Praxedes, Claveria, Sanchez-Mira, Pamplona, Abulug, Ballesteros, Aparri, Camalaniugan, Allacapan, Buguey, Santa Teresita, Santa Ana, Gonzaga, Lal-Lo, Lasam, Santo Niño, Piat, Tuao), the western portion of Nueva Vizcaya (Kayapa, Santa Fe, Ambaguio, Aritao, Bambang, Bayombong, Villaverde, Solano, Bagabag), and the northern portion of Zambales (Masinloc, Candelaria, Santa Cruz, Palauig, Iba)

Facts Recap: Baste filed a Travel Authority in June 2025 for a trip scheduled July 25–29. Baste issued a challenge to Torre on Saturday, July 19, during his “Basta Dabawenyo” program. His Travel Authority was approved on July 20. Torre accepted the challenge on Thursday, July 24. Venue preparations began on July 25. The DOST-PHIVOLCS, in collaboration with DOST XII, Office of Civil Defense (OCD) XII, Philippine Information Agency (PIA) XII, and Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG) XII, held its “PHIVOLCS InfoPress: Understanding and Communicating Geologic Hazards Information in Region XII” on July 29, 2025 at Greenleaf Hotel, General Santos City.
Mr. Abdul Jalil D. Malawan, Supervising Science Research Specialist (SRS) of DOST XII, welcomed the participants, composed of media practitioners, government information officers, and Disaster Risk Reduction frontliners across Central Mindanao.
Resource speakers from DOST-PHIVOLCS provided comprehensive discussions on volcano, earthquake, and tsunami information.
Mr. Jeffrey S. Perez, Supervising SRS, led a session on “Beneath the Surface: Understanding the Big One in Region XII.” Ms. Joan C. Salcedo, Supervising SRS, discussed a topic on “From Crest to Trough: Understanding the Science of Tsunami.”
Further, Ms. Charmaine V. Villamil, Senior SRS, shared an insight on “Land and Lava: Living with Active Volcanoes.” She also moderated the open forum to give the participants an opportunity to ask questions related to the topics.
In the afternoon, Mr. Christian R. Matullano, Information Officer II of PIA XII, talked about “#MagingMapanuri Campaign: Dismissing Disinformation.” Ms. Melissa Mae T. Garcia, SRS of DOST-PHIVOLCS, facilitated the “GeoTalks: Review of Commonly-used Geologic Terms”. Afterward, participants took part in a return demonstration workshop. Mr. Raylindo S. Aniñon, Regional Director of OCD XII, delivered his closing remarks.
Having experienced many earthquakes in the region for the past months, this event shares the mission in equipping our partners from the media in communicating the right information on geologic hazards and their impact on the community.

MAYNILA — Regular na nagsasagawa ng Simulation Exercise o SIMEX ang Special Weapons and Tactics o SWAT ng Manila Police District (MPD) para ihanda ang bawat miyembro sa mga darating nilang operasyon.
Ilan sa mga pagsasanay na ginagawa ang close quarter battle, stairway and hallway clearing at room entry. 
Kabilang ang mga ito sa mahahalagang hakbang na dapat nilang linagin lalo na sa mga kritikal na sitwasyon.Napakinabangan ito, halimbawa, sa pag-aaresto sa suspek sa pamamaril na hindi lumabas ng bahay.
Ayon sa tagapagsalita ng MPD na si Police Maj. Philipp Ines, paraan nila ito para masigurong alam nila ang gagawin sa kahit anumang scenario na makaharap nila. 
Tuloy-tuloy pa rin ang pag-eensayo ng SWAT sa kabila ng hindi magandang panahon.
– Ulat ni Jessie Cruzat, Patrol ng Pilipino

DISASTER RESPONSE UPDATE | PH-US AIR FORCES WORK HAND-IN-HAND TO CONTINUE DELIVERING AID IN BATANES
As part of ongoing Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Response (HADR) efforts in Northern Luzon, the United States Air Force (USAF) deployed its CV-22 Osprey aircraft to support the Philippine Air Force's (PAF) air assets in airlifting relief supplies to typhoon-affected communities in Basco, Batanes.
A total of 300 boxes of family food packs were airlifted aboard the USAF CV-22 Osprey, from Clark Air Base, Pampanga to Basco, Batanes. PAF personnel from the Tactical Operations Wing Northern Luzon (TOWNOL), provided essential ground support during the joint PH-US mission, assisting in the unloading, handling, and coordination of aid distribution in Basco, Batanes.
A day earlier, on July 29, 2025, the PAF deployed its C-130 and Black Hawk aircraft to transport batches of relief goods to Batanes and Abra, respectively. The C-130 aircraft also facilitated the transport of locally stranded individuals (LSIs) from Basco to Manila on its return flight. 
Source: Philippine Air Force

PANOORIN: Buwis-buhay na pagtawid sa ilog ang kailangang suungin ng mga residente sa  Brgy. Tinucan, Tanay, Rizal para lamang makarating sa bayan upang makapamili ng mga pagkain.
Kuwento ni YouScooper Rona Nikka Biason tungkol sa unang video rito na kinuha nitong July 23, isang lalaki ang hindi nag-alinlangan na magkabit ng lubid sa puno sa kabila ng ilog upang magkaroon ng balsa bilang pansamantalang transportasyon ng mga residente doon. 
"Sana mabigyang pansin ng ating gobyerno ang halos dekada na naming hinaing na sana kahit tulay na pantao lang ay malagyan ito," ayon kay Rona na kumuha ng video. 
Nakararanas umano sila ng biglang pagtaas ng tubig sa ilog dahilan upang umabot ng lampas-leeg hanggang lampas-tao ang taas nito. Makikita rito ang ilan pang video na pinadala ni YouScooper Rona na nangyari umano sa mga sumunod na araw, mula July 24 hanggang 26, 2025.
Dagdag ni Rona noong mga araw na iyon, mayroong tulay na maaaring daanan pero kailangan pa ring tumawid sa ilog, at mayroon ding ibang daanan pero may mga nakaharang na landslide.
Matapos magpadala ang GMA Integrated News noong July 25 ng paglagom ng hinaing ni YouScooper Rona at link patungo sa kaniyang video sa Facebook, sinabi ng Tanay LGU na inendorso na ang hinaing.
"Magalang po naming ipinababatid na amin pong naendorso ang naturang liham sa kinauukulang opisina para sa kinakailangang aksyon sa inyong hinaing," sinabi ni Dr. Jeffrey Pino, municipal administrator ng Tanay, Rizal, nitong July 31 sa pamamagitan ng email. #Youscoop

National Grid Corp. of the Philippines (NGCP) is placing the Visayas and Mindanao grids on yellow alert due to power plant outages and high system demand.
Effective Friday, Aug. 1, from 6 to 8 p.m., the two regions will be put on a yellow alert—an advisory issued when the operating margin is insufficient to meet the grid’s contingency requirement. According to NGCP’s report, the available capacity in Visayas is at 2,569 megawatts (MW), while its peak demand is at 2,449 MW.
“A total of 423 MW [is] unavailable to the grid,” it said.

WHERE IS THE PRESIDENT NOW?
While Typhoon Crising lashes the Philippines, leaving entire towns flooded, homes destroyed, and Filipinos crying for help, our President is abroad—comfortably meeting with the US President.
 This is leadership?
In the face of calamity, when his people need him the most, he chooses to leave. No direct presence, no leadership on the ground. Just silence. Is this the kind of leader we deserve?
Under the 1987 Philippine Constitution, the President is the Commander-in-Chief and must be present and accountable in times of national emergency. Leaving the country without declaring who is in command violates his constitutional duties.
 LEGAL BASIS: 
 Article VII, Section 4 – The President shall ensure the faithful execution of the laws and must uphold accountability to the people.
 Article XI, Section 1 – Public officers, including the President, must at all times be accountable to the people.
 Article XI, Section 2 – The President may be removed from office on impeachment for culpable violation of the Constitution, betrayal of public trust, or gross neglect of duty.
 Abandoning the nation during a declared State of Calamity without properly delegating emergency authority can be considered gross negligence and betrayal of public trust.
Is this the kind of leader we want — one who leaves during disaster? Or do we deserve someone who will stand and lead in the storm?

DISASTER RESPONSE UPDATE | BATANES RELIEF MISSION WRAPS UP WITH FINAL AIRLIFT OF 1,500 FOOD PACKS
In support of ongoing Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Response (HADR) efforts in the province of Batanes, two U.S. Air Force CV-22 Osprey aircraft and two U.S. Marine Corps MV-22 Osprey aircraft transported a total of 1,500 Family Food Packs (FFPs) provided by the Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) on August 3, 2025.
The relief mission, which began on July 28, 2025, was spearheaded by the Office of Civil Defense (OCD) and mobilized both Philippine and U.S. air assets to deliver critical aid to typhoon-affected and geographically isolated communities in Northern Luzon. Over the course of seven days, a total of 6,300 food packs were airlifted from Clark Air Base in Pampanga to Basco, Batanes, utilizing combined PH–U.S airlift capabilities.
Source: Philippine Air Force

Cocolife Area Head for Mindanao Darwin Calvo and Regional Trainer Ralfh Bascon also introduced the company’s newest insurance offerings: Cocolife Agapay and Cocolife Kalinga.
Cocolife Agapay is a flexible life and health insurance plan with investment growth, ideal for Filipinos seeking long-term security and value. Meanwhile, Cocolife Kalinga offers affordable term insurance with critical illness coverage and daily hospital income benefits, perfect for those looking for essential, no-fuss protection.
The event also marked the official launch of the Cocolife Run Club, aimed at promoting a healthier, more active lifestyle among Filipinos.
To learn more, follow Cocolife on facebook or visit their website at www.cocolife.com.

Ukraine’s envoy to Manila is calling for intensified international action, warning that without it, Russia’s indiscriminate drone and missile assaults could be condoned, and the conflict risks becoming a "forgotten war."
The deadliest drone and missile strike on Kyiv in over a year, involving more than 300 drones and eight missiles, claimed 28 lives, including three children, and injured over 150, according to official figures reported by Ukrainian authorities .
Speaking to ANC's Headstart, Ambassador Yuliia Fediv described civilian life in Kyiv as “like Russian roulette,” saying nightly strikes force families to live in constant fear. She argued sanctions must be broadened to include Russia's trading partners, whom she blamed for helping Moscow “produce more weapons”.
With Ukraine’s population now around 38.98 million -- down significantly from over 52 million in 1991 -- Fediv cautioned that demographic decline, war casualties, and migration amplify the need for swift resolution and justice.
She reiterated that while Ukraine supports diplomacy, it sees “no real intention” from Moscow to negotiate -- unless global pressure mounts . Moreover, she said peace this year would not only end suffering in Ukraine but also serve as a precedent: "if you break international law, you will be punished,” reinforcing the rule‑based order especially in the Indo‑Pacific.
Fediv also highlighted deepening Ukraine‑Philippines collaboration -- from defense dialogue to shared cultural projects -- and stressed their mutual commitment to faith and family values. — Raine Musñgi, ABS‑CBN News Channel Ukraine’s envoy to Manila is calling for intensified international action, warning that without it, Russia’s indiscriminate drone and missile assaults could be condoned, and the conflict risks becoming a "forgotten war." SYNOPSIS:
At 3:00 PM today, the Low Pressure Area (LPA) was estimated based on all available data at 570 km East of Virac, Catanduanes (14.4°N, 129.4°E). Southwest Monsoon affecting Mindanao, and the western sections of Southern Luzon and Visayas.
FORECAST:
Davao Region will experience partly cloudy to cloudy skies with isolated rainshowers or thunderstorms due to Southwest Monsoon. Possible flash floods or landslides during severe thunderstorms. Light to moderate winds coming from Southwest will prevail with slight to moderate seas (0.6 to 2.1 meters wave height).

Ang Dakbayan sa Davao ug ubang dapit sa Davao Region makasinati sa panalagsang pagdag-um ngadto sa madag-umon nga kalangitan na inubanan sa pat-ak pat-ak nga pag-ulan kilat ug pagpanalugdog kasagari sa hapon ug gabi-i tungod sa Habagat. LOOK: A 62-year-old hobbyist wildlife photographer from Iloilo showcased his mesmerizing wildlife shots, highlighting endangered birds in the Philippines. 
Raymond Garibay Miñoso shared with the Inquirer that he started three years ago as a macro photographer, taking insects on a piece of property inherited from his parents, and eventually shifted his focus to birds.
Some of his shots include the majestic Philippine Eagle taken at the Philippine Eagle Center in Davao, the rare Yellow-faced flameback, and the Visayan hornbill shot in Antique. 
Miñoso also noted that taking photographs of endangered birds helps raise awareness, supports conservation, and inspires people to protect these irreplaceable species.

As part of its commitment in championing volcano, earthquake, and tsunami disaster risk reduction (DRR) activities, DOST-PHIVOLCS leads a “Training on Communicating PHIVOLCS Information Materials and Tools for School DRR Focal Persons of the Department of Education (DepEd) Davao Occidental” from August 5-7, 2025 at Sun City Suites, General Santos City.
In his message, Dr. Teresito C. Bacolcol, Director of DOST-PHIVOLCS, emphasized the vital role of DRR focal persons in every school, facilitating the conduct of evacuation drills, checking safety plans, and hazard information awareness.
“Your work may not always be seen, but it makes a big difference. We hope that this training gives you something useful to bring back. And more than anything, we hope it reminds you that what you do matters–quietly, steadily, and every single day,” Dr. Bacolcol added.
Participants learned various topics related to volcanoes, earthquakes, and tsunami information from DOST-PHIVOLCS resource speakers.
Ms. Fatima M. Moncada, Science Research Specialist (SRS) II, discussed key principles in “DRRM Laws and Frameworks; Child Rights Convention; Understanding Hazards and Disasters."
Ms. Lucille Rose D. Sanico, Senior SRS, shared the overview of “Volcanic Eruption Hazards and Impacts." She also imparted her insights on “Understanding Volcano Alert Level Scheme" and “What to do Before, During and After a Volcanic Eruption.”
A learning activity on “Precursory Signs of an Impending Volcanic Eruption” assessed the takeaways of the participants on the given discussions.
Ms. Joan C. Salcedo, Supervising SRS, tackled the “Overview of Earthquake Hazards and Impacts.”
Lastly, Ms. Moncada lectured on “Landslide Preparedness” to the participants.
Being situated in an area vulnerable to earthquakes, this workshop is an opportunity to empower teachers and DRR focal persons in Davao Occidental in responding to geologic hazards through science-based DRR initiatives and relay these skills to their students and community.

, Zamboanga del Norte (6), Zamboanga Sibugay (1), Zamboanga City’s ZCDRRMO and City Engineer’s Office (3), Isabela City (3), and the Department of Agriculture (1).

K9 DOG UNDER REHABILITATION
A Belgian Malinois K9 named Kobe is undergoing a two- to three-month rehabilitation period with the Animal Kingdom Foundation (AKF). The foundation took custody of the police dog after photos of him, looking emaciated, went viral online and caused public concern.
On a Facebook post on Tuesday, August 5, AKF said they sent a formal request urging an investigation into Kobe's condition and the welfare of all K9 units under government custody.
On August 4, the Regional Explosive and Canine Unit-NCR visited AKF to discuss Kobe's condition. They said Kobe was recently relocated from Taguig to Manila, had just finished refresher training, and was newly paired with his handler, who is a person with a disability.
Officials added that Kobe's lab results were normal, his vaccinations were up to date, and he was being fed properly.
"While we thank the RECU, EOD- K9 and the MPD for their immediate response in reaching out, we continue to call for an urgent and comprehensive review of the health and welfare of all working K9s. In recognizing their indispensable and physically demanding role in protecting lives and detecting dangers,  the K9 heroes deserve better working condition and care," the Animal Kingdom Foundation said in a post. | via SunStar Cebu

DALAWANG LPA SA LOOB AT LABAS NG PAR, PATULOY NGAYONG BINABANTAYAN 
Ang unang LPA (08a) na nasa silangan ng #Quezon ay patuloy na kumikilos papalapit sa landmass ng #Luzon. Inaasahang tuluyan na itong magla-landfall bukas ng gabi at inaasahang tatawirin ang kalupaan ng #NorthernLuzon hanggang sa Biyernes ng umaga.
Inaasahang bahagya rin nitong hahatakin ang #Habagat na inaasahang magdadala ng mga kalat-kalat na pag-ulan sa bansa partikular sa kanlurang bahagi.
Samantala, isa pang panibagong LPA (08b) ang nabuo sa labas ng PAR o sa silangan ng #NorthernLuzon at may tsansang pumasok ng PAR at maging bagyo sa mga susunod na araw. 
Sakaling maging bagyo ito pagpasok ng PAR, tatawagin itong #FabianPH.
Patuloy na babantayan ang magiging kilos nito dahil hindi rin inaalis ang posibilidad na lumapit ito sa #NorthernLuzon next week.
Manatiling mag-antabay ng mga susunod pang update hinggil sa mga nasabing sama ng panahon sa mga susunod na araw.
— PWS/PSU

The Luzon leg of Handa Pilipinas sa Bagong Pilipinas Innovations in Climate and Disaster Resilience Nationwide Exposition 2025 officially kicks off today hosted by the Department of Science and Technology- Cordillera Administrative Region (DOST-CAR) with the theme “Bida and Handa: STI for a Smart and Resilient Luzon” back-to-back with the Regional Science and Technology Week (RSTW) in CAR at the Newtown Plaza Hotel, Baguio City on August 7-9, 2025.
The ceremonial Memorandum of Agreement (MOA) signing of the GeoRiskPh Adoption by the Cordillera Regional Land Use Committee (RLUC) happened during the opening ceremony signed by DOST-PHIVOLCS Director Dr. Teresito C. Bacolcol, RLUC Chairperson Dir. Apollo Edwin S. Pagano, and DOST-CAR Regional Director Dr. Nancy A Bantog witnessed by DOST Secretary Dr. Renato U. Solidum, DOST Undersecretary for Regional Operations Engr. Sancho A. Mabborang, and DHSUD-CAR Regional Director Marvin M. Feraren. 
Also, the Seismic Hazard Atlas under Seismic Hazard Assessment for the Design Earthquake of the Philippines (SHADE) Project was presented and turned over by DOST Officials, Cordillera Regional Disaster Risk Reduction and Management (RDRRMC) Officials, and CAR Local Government Unit (LGU) Officials.

Severe Tropical Storm PODUL

Valid for broadcast until the next bulletin at 11:00 PM today.
SEVERE TROPICAL STORM “PODUL” CONTINUES TO ACCELERATE WHILE MAINTAINING ITS STRENGTH.

The center of Severe Tropical Storm PODUL was estimated based on all available data at 1,680 km East of Extreme Northern Luzon (OUTSIDE PAR) (21.7°N, 138.0°E).
• Intensity
Maximum sustained winds of 110 km/h near the center, gustiness of up to 135 km/h, and central pressure of 985 hPa.
• Present Movement
Westward at 25 km/h
• Extent of Tropical Cyclone Winds
Strong to storm-force winds extend outwards up to 280 km from the center
GENERAL OUTLOOK FOR THE FORECAST PERIOD
• PODUL is less likely to directly affect the weather and sea conditions in the country within the next five days.
• PODUL is forecast to move generally westward today and tomorrow (11 August), then west northwestward or northwestward from Tuesday (12 August) through the end of the forecast period. PODUL may enter the Philippine Area of Responsibility between tonight and tomorrow early morning. On the track forecast, PODUL may pass close or over the southern Ryukyu Islands on Wednesday (13 August) morning. Furthermore, a landfall scenario over Taiwan on Wednesday afternoon or evening is also not ruled out.
• There is large uncertainty in the projected track and intensity of PODUL from Monday through the end of the forecast period since any northward or southward shift in the track forecast will significantly change the intensity forecast. All are advised to continue monitoring subsequent tropical cyclone advisories for PODUL.
Considering these developments, the public and disaster risk reduction and management offices concerned are advised to continue monitoring for updates related to this tropical cyclone. 
Unless there is an intermediate issuance, the next tropical cyclone advisory will be issued at 11:00 PM today.

TROPICAL CYCLONE ADVISORY NR. 5
Severe Tropical Storm PODUL
Issued at 11:00 AM, 10 August 2025
Valid for broadcast until the next bulletin at 11:00 PM today.
SEVERE TROPICAL STORM “PODUL” CONTINUES TO ACCELERATE WHILE MAINTAINING ITS STRENGTH.
• Location of Center (10:00 AM)
The center of Severe Tropical Storm PODUL was estimated based on all available data at 1,680 km East of Extreme Northern Luzon (OUTSIDE PAR) (21.7°N, 138.0°E).
• Intensity
Maximum sustained winds of 110 km/h near the center, gustiness of up to 135 km/h, and central pressure of 985 hPa.
• Present Movement
Westward at 25 km/h
• Extent of Tropical Cyclone Winds
Strong to storm-force winds extend outwards up to 280 km from the center
GENERAL OUTLOOK FOR THE FORECAST PERIOD
• PODUL is less likely to directly affect the weather and sea conditions in the country within the next five days.
• PODUL is forecast to move generally westward today and tomorrow (11 August), then west northwestward or northwestward from Tuesday (12 August) through the end of the forecast period. PODUL may enter the Philippine Area of Responsibility between tonight and tomorrow early morning. On the track forecast, PODUL may pass close or over the southern Ryukyu Islands on Wednesday (13 August) morning. Furthermore, a landfall scenario over Taiwan on Wednesday afternoon or evening is also not ruled out.
• There is large uncertainty in the projected track and intensity of PODUL from Monday through the end of the forecast period since any northward or southward shift in the track forecast will significantly change the intensity forecast. All are advised to continue monitoring subsequent tropical cyclone advisories for PODUL.
Considering these developments, the public and disaster risk reduction and management offices concerned are advised to continue monitoring for updates related to this tropical cyclone. 
Unless there is an intermediate issuance, the next tropical cyclone advisory will be issued at 11:00 PM today.

TAAL VOLCANO ADVISORY
10 August 2025
2:00 PM
This is a notice of increased seismic energy release from Taal Volcano.
Since 05:25 AM today, 10 August 2025, stations of the Taal Volcano Network (TVN) situated on Taal Volcano Island (TVI) have been recording a pronounced increase in real-time seismic energy measurement, or RSAM, simultaneous with continuing volcanic tremor. A total of nineteen (19) volcanic earthquakes has been recorded by the TVN since 09 August 2025. Visual observations noted a moderate to voluminous plume from the Taal Main Crater since the start of RSAM increase. Taal has been degassing low levels of sulfur dioxide or SO2 since June 2025 with the latest emission measured on 8 August 2025, averaging 374 tonnes/day. These sharp increase in RSAM and vigorous steaming from the Main Crater may lead to a phreatic or even a minor phreatomagmatic eruption.
DOST-PHIVOLCS reminds the public that Alert Level 1 prevails over Taal Volcano, which means that it is still in abnormal condition and should not be interpreted to have ceased unrest nor ceased the threat of eruptive activity. At Alert Level 1, sudden steam-driven or phreatic or minor phreatomagmatic eruptions, minor ashfall and lethal accumulations or expulsions of volcanic gas can occur and threaten areas within TVI. DOST-PHIVOLCS strongly recommends that entry into TVI, Taal’s Permanent Danger Zone or PDZ, especially the vicinities of the Main Crater and the Daang Kastila fissure, must remain strictly prohibited. Local government units are advised to continuously prepare for potential recurrence of volcanic SO2 increases and exposure of their communities and undertake appropriate response measures to mitigate the health impacts of these hazards. Lastly, civil aviation authorities must also advise pilots to avoid flying above TVI as ash from any sudden eruption can be hazardous to aircraft.
DOST-PHIVOLCS is closely monitoring Taal Volcano’s activity and any new significant development will be immediately communicated to all stakeholders.

TROPICAL CYCLONE ADVISORY NR. 5
Severe Tropical Storm PODUL
Issued at 11:00 AM, 10 August 2025
Valid for broadcast until the next bulletin at 11:00 PM today.
SEVERE TROPICAL STORM “PODUL” CONTINUES TO ACCELERATE WHILE MAINTAINING ITS STRENGTH.
• Location of Center (10:00 AM)
The center of Severe Tropical Storm PODUL was estimated based on all available data at 1,680 km East of Extreme Northern Luzon (OUTSIDE PAR) (21.7°N, 138.0°E).
• Intensity
Maximum sustained winds of 110 km/h near the center, gustiness of up to 135 km/h, and central pressure of 985 hPa.
• Present Movement
Westward at 25 km/h
• Extent of Tropical Cyclone Winds
Strong to storm-force winds extend outwards up to 280 km from the center
GENERAL OUTLOOK FOR THE FORECAST PERIOD
• PODUL is less likely to directly affect the weather and sea conditions in the country within the next five days.
• PODUL is forecast to move generally westward today and tomorrow (11 August), then west northwestward or northwestward from Tuesday (12 August) through the end of the forecast period. PODUL may enter the Philippine Area of Responsibility between tonight and tomorrow early morning. On the track forecast, PODUL may pass close or over the southern Ryukyu Islands on Wednesday (13 August) morning. Furthermore, a landfall scenario over Taiwan on Wednesday afternoon or evening is also not ruled out.
• There is large uncertainty in the projected track and intensity of PODUL from Monday through the end of the forecast period since any northward or southward shift in the track forecast will significantly change the intensity forecast. All are advised to continue monitoring subsequent tropical cyclone advisories for PODUL.
Considering these developments, the public and disaster risk reduction and management offices concerned are advised to continue monitoring for updates related to this tropical cyclone. 
Unless there is an intermediate issuance, the next tropical cyclone advisory will be issued at 11:00 PM today.

TAAL VOLCANO ADVISORY
This is a notice of increased seismic energy release from Taal Volcano.
Since 05:25 AM today, 10 August 2025, stations of the Taal Volcano Network (TVN) situated on Taal Volcano Island (TVI) have been recording a pronounced increase in real-time seismic energy measurement, or RSAM, simultaneous with continuing volcanic tremor. 
A total of nineteen (19) volcanic earthquakes has been recorded by the TVN since 09 August 2025. Visual observations noted a moderate to voluminous plume from the Taal Main Crater since the start of RSAM increase. 
Taal has been degassing low levels of sulfur dioxide or SO2 since June 2025 with the latest emission measured on 8 August 2025, averaging 374 tonnes/day. These sharp increase in RSAM and vigorous steaming from the Main Crater may lead to a phreatic or even a minor phreatomagmatic eruption.
Source: Philippine Institute of Volcanology and Seismology (PHIVOLCS-DOST)

TROPICAL CYCLONE ADVISORY NR. 5
Severe Tropical Storm PODUL
Issued at 11:00 AM, 10 August 2025
Valid for broadcast until the next bulletin at 11:00 PM today.
SEVERE TROPICAL STORM “PODUL” CONTINUES TO ACCELERATE WHILE MAINTAINING ITS STRENGTH.
• Location of Center (10:00 AM)
The center of Severe Tropical Storm PODUL was estimated based on all available data at 1,680 km East of Extreme Northern Luzon (OUTSIDE PAR) (21.7°N, 138.0°E).
• Intensity
Maximum sustained winds of 110 km/h near the center, gustiness of up to 135 km/h, and central pressure of 985 hPa.
• Present Movement
Westward at 25 km/h
• Extent of Tropical Cyclone Winds
Strong to storm-force winds extend outwards up to 280 km from the center
GENERAL OUTLOOK FOR THE FORECAST PERIOD
• PODUL is less likely to directly affect the weather and sea conditions in the country within the next five days.
• PODUL is forecast to move generally westward today and tomorrow (11 August), then west northwestward or northwestward from Tuesday (12 August) through the end of the forecast period. PODUL may enter the Philippine Area of Responsibility between tonight and tomorrow early morning. On the track forecast, PODUL may pass close or over the southern Ryukyu Islands on Wednesday (13 August) morning. Furthermore, a landfall scenario over Taiwan on Wednesday afternoon or evening is also not ruled out.
• There is large uncertainty in the projected track and intensity of PODUL from Monday through the end of the forecast period since any northward or southward shift in the track forecast will significantly change the intensity forecast. All are advised to continue monitoring subsequent tropical cyclone advisories for PODUL.
Considering these developments, the public and disaster risk reduction and management offices concerned are advised to continue monitoring for updates related to this tropical cyclone. 
Unless there is an intermediate issuance, the next tropical cyclone advisory will be issued at 11:00 PM today.

At 3:00 AM today, the center of the eye of Typhoon "GORIO" {PODUL} was estimated based on all available data at 190 km Northeast of Itbayat, Batanes (21.9N, 123.2E) with maximum sustained winds of 140 km/h near the center and gustiness of up to 170 km/h. It is moving West Northwestward at 25 km/h. Southwest Monsoon affecting the western sections Mindanao.
FORECAST:
Zamboanga Peninsula, BARMM, and SOCCSKSARGEN will have cloudy skies with scattered rains and thunderstorms due to Southwest Monsoon. Possibe flash floods or landslides due to moderate to at times heavy rains. The rest of Mindanao will have partly cloudy to cloudy skies with isolated rainshowers or thunderstorms due to Localized Thunderstoms. Light to moderate winds from Southwest with slight to moderate seas (0.6 to 1.5 meters).

Ang Zamboanga Peninsula, BARMM ug SOCCSKSARGEN makasinati sa mapanganuron nga kalangitan inubanan sa katag katag nga mga pag-ulan, kilat ug pagpanalugdog tungod sa Southwest Monsoon. Posible ang mga pagbaha o pagdahili sa yuta tungod sa kasarangan ngadto na sa usahay kusog nga mga pag-ulan. Samtang ang ubang dapit sa Mindanao makasinati sa panalagsang pagdag-um ngadto sa mapanganuron nga kalangitan inubanan sa pat-ak pat-ak nga pag-ulan, kilat ug pagpanalugdog tungod sa Localized Thunderstorms. Hinay ngadto sa kasarangan nga hangin ang magagikan sa habagatang kasadpang direksyon ug ang kadagatan hapsay ngadto sa kasarangan ang pagbalud.

Issued at   4:00 AM  AUGUST  14, 2025 
Valid Until 4:00 AM Tomorrow
SYNOPSIS: Southwest Monsoon affecting the country. Localized Thunderstorms affecting Davao Region.

SEVERE TROPICAL STORM PODUL(2511) (FORMERLY  “GORIO”)
LOCATION: 650 KM NORTHWEST OF EXTREME NORTHERN LUZON (24.3 N-116.8 E)
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS: 95 KPH NEAR THE CENTER
GUSTINESS: UP TO160 KPH
MOVEMENT: WEST NORTHWESTWARD AT 35 KPH
FORECAST:
Davao Oriental will experience cloudy skies with scattered rains and thunderstorms due to Southwest Monsoon. Possible flash floods or landslides due to moderate to at times heavy rains. The rest of Davao Region will have partly cloudy to cloudy skies with isolated rainshowers or thunderstorms due to Localized Thunderstorms. Possible flash floods or landslides during severe thunderstorms. Light to moderate wind coming from the Southwest will prevail and the coastal waters will be slight to moderate.

Ang Davao Oriental makasinati ug madag umun nga kalangitan inubanan sa KATAG KATAG nga pagulan, kilat ug pagpanalugdug tungod sa Southwest Monsoon O Hangin Habagat. Posible ang pagbaha ug pagdahili sa yuta kung adunay masinati nga kasarangan ngadto sa kusug nga pag ulan. Nag-atubang og daghang warrants of arrest sa Regional Trial Court (RTC) Branch 10 sa siyudad sa Davao ang kanhing pulis nga si Arturo Lascañas tungod sa mga kasong online libel, murder, ug attempted murder.
Labing uwahing warrant ni Lascañas mao ang online libel pinetsahan Hunyo 9, 2025 nga may pyansang P48,000.
Mga una niyang warrants, mao ang tungod sa kasong murder, pinetsahan Oktubre 16, 2020 nga wa’y pyansa. Laing kaso mai ang attempted murder nga may bail nga P120,000.
Sa maong mga warrants, ang mga otoridad, gimanduan nga ipatuman kini sud sa 10 ka adlaw ug kinahanglang may pagpasabot kung ugaling mapakyas sa pagpatuman ang mga hingtungdan.
Ang mga warrants, naka-address sa mga posibleng gipuy-an ni Lascañas sa Bariquit Compound, Sitio San Andres, Brgy. Indangan, Davao City ug Roseville Subdivision, Buhangin, Davao City.
Kahinumduman nga si Lascañas, mipasiatab nga miyembro siya sa Davao Death Squad, ug alegasyong misibat pagawas sa nasud ug mitestigo batok former President Rodrigo Duterte.

MINDANAO WEATHER FORECAST #MINPRSD
ISSUED AT: 5:00 PM 15 August 2025
VALID UNTIL: 5:00 PM Tomorrow
SYNOPSIS: Southwest Monsoon affecting Zamboanga Peninsula. Localized Thunderstorms affecting rest of Mindanao.
FORECAST:
Zamboanga Peninsula will have cloudy skies with scattered rains and thunderstorms due to Southwest Monsoon. Possible flash floods or landslides due to moderate to at times heavy rains. Rest of Mindanao will be partly cloudy to cloudy with isolated rainshowers or thunderstorms due to Localized Thunderstorms. Light to moderate winds from south to southwest with slight to moderate seas (0.6 to 1.8 meters).
KAUGALINGONG DAYALEKTO:
Ang Zamboanga Peninsula makasinati sa mapanganuron nga kalangitan inubanan sa katag katag nga mga pag-ulan, kilat ug pagpanalugdog tungod sa Southwest Monsoon. Posible ang mga pagbaha o pagdahili sa yuta tungod sa kasarangan ngadto na sa usahay kusog nga mga pag-ulan. Ang ubang dapit sa Mindanao makasinati sa panalagsang pagdag-um ngadto sa mapanganuron nga kalangitan inubanan sa pat-ak pat-ak nga pag-ulan, kilat ug pagpanalugdog tungod sa Localized Thunderstorms. Hinay ngadto sa kasarangan nga hangin ang magagikan sa habagatang ngadto sa habagatang kasadpang nga direksyon ug ang kadagatan hapsay ngadto sa kasarangan ang pagbalud.

Southwest Monsoon affecting the western section of Southern Luzon.
Localized Thunderstorms affecting Davao Region.
FORECAST:
DAVAO REGION will experience partly cloudy to cloudy skies with isolated rainshowers and thunderstorms due Localized Thunderstorms. Possible flashfloods or landslides during severe thunderstorms. 
Light to Moderate winds coming from the Southeast to Northeast will prevail and the coastal waters will be Slight to Moderate. 
(0.6 to 1.2 meters wave height)

Contractors for flood control projects across the Philippines appeared before the Senate Blue Ribbon Committee on Tuesday, August 19, 2025, for a probe into the nation’s flood management issues.
Alan Quirante of QM Builders, a Cebu-based development firm, was among the seven contractors who attended the inquiry. Four other contractors sent representatives, while seven more were absent but submitted written replies.
The Senate hearing followed a report from the Presidential Communications Office (PCO), released on August 11, which ranked Cebu second nationwide in the number of flood control projects despite not being among the country’s top 10 flood-prone provinces.
Based on the National Adaptation Plan of the Philippines 2023–2050, Cebu recorded 414 completed and ongoing flood control projects between July 2022 and May 2025 -- second only to Bulacan. Nationwide, a total of 9,855 projects are in place, amounting to more than P545 billion.
QM Builders is currently ranked as the country’s fourth-largest contractor. The PCO report stemmed from President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.’s directive during his June 28, 2025, State of the Nation Address. | via SunStar Cebu

The Office of Civil Defense XI has formally signed a Memorandum of Agreement (MOA) with the municipalities of Jose Abad Santos, Don Marcelino, Boston, and Governor Generoso for the prepositioning of Non-Food Items (NFIs), ensuring that families in disaster-prone and hard-to-reach communities can receive immediate assistance when emergencies strike.
Held at the OCD XI Conference Room last August 5, 7, and 13–14, 2025, the ceremonial signing marks another step in bringing life-saving relief closer to the ground. By strategically storing essential NFIs within local government facilities, OCD XI and its partner LGUs are reducing response time, improving accessibility, and enhancing the effectiveness of humanitarian assistance and disaster response.
This initiative advances the goals of the Philippine Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Act of 2010 (RA 10121), particularly in strengthening preparedness, improving response readiness, and building community resilience.
OCD XI commends the local chief executives and representatives for their commitment to this partnership, which demonstrates a whole-of-government and whole-of-nation approach in safeguarding lives and protecting communities.
Similar MOA signings will follow with the municipalities of Sarangani, Laak, and Maragusan, broadening collaboration across the Davao Region to ensure more communities are supported and prepared for disaster response.

WATCH: KC Concepcion expresses her gratitude to the United Nations World Food Programme (WFP), sharing how the organization shaped her perspective on hunger and nutrition, and how it influences the broader education crisis in the country.
The award-winning actress and entrepreneur was officially announced as WFP Goodwill Ambassador on Tuesday, August 19, at WFP's headquarters in Mandaluyong.
She will be working side by side with the organization in its efforts to provide universal school meals across impoverished regions in the Philippines, while also expanding WFP’s global advocacy of ending world hunger.

Samantala, isa pang kumpol ng kaulapan ang nabuo sa Pacific Ocean na posibleng maging bagong sama ng panahon o LPA sa mga susunod na araw at patuloy na babantayan.
Manatiling mag-monitor ng mga susunod na update hinggil sa nasabing mga weather system dahil posible pa rin ang mga pagbabago rito.

BINABANTAYANG LPA SA PACIFIC OCEAN, NAGBABADYA NANG PUMASOK NG PAR BUKAS 
Matapos lumabas ng PAR kaninang umaga ang Tropical Depression #HuaningPH na ngayo’y papalapit na sa #Japan, nagbabadya namang pumasok ng PAR bukas ang isa pang LPA na patuloy na binabantayan.
Hindi inaalis ang tsansa na lumakas ito bilang bagyo at inaasahang lalapit at tatawid ng #NorthernLuzon o #CentralLuzon sa weekend.
Sakaling maging bagyo, tatawagin itong #IsangPH.
Inaasahang bahagya rin nitong hahatakin ang #Habagat na muling magdadala ng kalat-kalat na pag-ulan partikular sa kanlurang bahagi ng bansa sa mga susunod na araw.
Samantala, isa pang kumpol ng kaulapan ang nabuo sa Pacific Ocean na posibleng maging bagong sama ng panahon o LPA sa mga susunod na araw at patuloy na babantayan.
Manatiling mag-monitor ng mga susunod na update hinggil sa nasabing mga weather system dahil posible pa rin ang mga pagbabago rito.
— PWS/PSU

Heavy clouds of smoke billowing from wildfires filled the sky over mountains and hills in northern and western Spain on Tuesday (August 19), as the end of a two-week heatwave and expected rainfall have fanned hopes that an end may be in sight.
Data on Tuesday from the European Forest Fire Information System showed the fires have burned vegetation on 38,000 hectares (94,000 acres) since Monday (August 18), just below 42,000 hectares during the whole of 2024.
Videos shot by the 43rd unit of the Spanish Aerial Forces showed wildfires seen from the sky in the western province of Caceres and the northwestern province of Leon.
Spain’s national weather agency, which on Monday (August 18) declared the end of one of the longest heatwaves in the past five decades, now expects temperatures to fall and humidity to rise. The Regional Director of the Bureau of Fire Protection Regional Office XI, FCSUPT JUNITO F MASLANG, DSC, conducted an official visit to the Digos City Fire Station to evaluate the Urban Agriculture and Green Space Program.

Heavy Rainfall Outlook

• Sunday (24 August): Kalayaan Islands.

24-Hour Sea Condition Outlook

Up to moderate seas over the following coastal waters:
• Up to 2.5 m: The seaboards of Isabela, Ilocos Norte, and Ilocos Sur.
• Up to 2.0 m: The seaboard of Aurora and Zambales; the western seaboards of Bataan and Lubang Island.
• Mariners of motorbancas and similarly-sized vessels are advised to take precautionary measures while venturing out to sea and, if possible, avoid navigation under these conditions.
TRACK AND INTENSITY OUTLOOK
• Tropical Depression ISANG will move generally westward during the forecast period. On the track forecast, it will traverse Northern Luzon in the next 12 hours, emerge over the West Philippine Sea tonight, and eventually exit the Philippine Area of Responsibility tomorrow (23 August) morning or afternoon.
• ISANG is forecast to intensify into a tropical storm tomorrow morning and may reach severe tropical storm category while approach the waters south of Hainan, China. However, intensification into a tropical storm at a much earlier time (e.g., several hours after emerging over the West Philippine Sea) is not ruled out.
Considering these developments, the public and disaster risk reduction and management offices concerned are advised to take all necessary measures to protect life and property. Persons living in areas identified to be highly or very highly susceptible to these hazards are advised to follow evacuation and other instructions from local officials. For heavy rainfall warnings, thunderstorm/rainfall advisories, and other severe weather information specific to your area, please monitor products issued by your local PAGASA Regional Services Division.

ICYMI: In line with the installation and integration of the 94th Community Tsunami Alerting Station (CTAS) in Tarragona, Davao Oriental, DOST-PHIVOLCS, in partnership with the Municipal Government of Tarragona and DOST Region XI - Davao Oriental, conducted an Information, Education, and Communication (IEC) campaign and Workshop on Tsunami Evacuation on August 21, 2025 at the Municipal Gym, Barangay Central, Tarragona, Davao Oriental. 
DOST-Provincial Science and Technology Office Director Mirasol G. Domingo sent her support through the Community Empowerment through Science and Technology (CEST) Program. Mr. Dennis D. Awing of  MDRRMO Tarragona delivered the welcome remarks on behalf of Mayor Art Benjie C. Bulaong. 
Participants from municipal offices and barangays learned the fundamentals of earthquake and tsunami generation through a presentation by Mr. Joymar C. Bomboc, Science Research Assistant. Moreover, Ms. Jordana Marie L. Argamosa, Science Research Analyst, delivered an overview on the Earthquake and Tsunami Alerting Module (ETAM) and Tsunami Simulation and Impact Module (TsuSIM) of the Rapid Earthquake Damage Assessment System (REDAS) software. Engr.  Angelito G. Lanuza, Supervising Science Research Specialist (SRS), discussed the PHIVOLCS Earthquake Intensity Scale (PEIS) and the natural signs of an impending local tsunami, while Mr. Nico B. Anilao, Project Technical Aide VI, presented the Philippine Tsunami Network and Tsunami Early Warning System (TeWS) visualization.
To fully understand the role of community participation in disaster preparedness, Ms. Joan C. Salcedo, Supervising SRS, introduced the community-based early warning system (CBEWS), the 12 indicators for Tsunami Ready Recognition Program, and how to conduct a tsunami drill. Participants were able to appreciate the importance of their contribution through a workshop on crafting their own initial tsunami evacuation maps with information needed for their tsunami evacuation plans, which will guide them on the routes to the designated safe evacuation site in the shortest time possible.

It is moving West northwestward at 15 km/h. Southwest Monsoon affecting Mindanao.
FORECAST:
Mindanao will have partly cloudy to cloudy skies with isolated rainshowers or thunderstorms due to Southwest Monsoon. Possible flash floods or landslides during severe thunderstorms. Light to moderate winds from west to northwest with slight to moderate seas (0.6 to 1.5 meters).

In response to the ongoing earthquake swarm near the borders of Camarines Sur and Camarines Norte, the Department of Science and Technology–Philippine Institute of Volcanology and Seismology (DOST-PHIVOLCS) has deployed a Quick Response Team (QRT) since August 15, 2025.
The team, composed of experts from the Guinayangan Seismic Station, Tagaytay Mirror Station, and PHIVOLCS Main Office, installed four (4) portable seismic stations at the Camarines Sur Emergency Operations Center (EOC), Libmanan EOC and Siruma Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office (DRRMO), both in Camarines Sur, and in Daet, Camarines Norte. The additional stations will augment DOST-PHIVOLCS’ earthquake monitoring network, thus improving the accuracy of earthquake information and expanding real-time data coverage.
DOST-PHIVOLCS is closely working with the Local Government Units (LGUs) through the Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Offices (DRRMOs), during the briefings and coordination. Information, Education, and Communication (IEC) campaigns were conducted in affected communities where IEC materials were also distributed.
PHIVOLCS urges the public to stay informed through official channels and to follow safety protocols at all times.

DOST-PAGASA S & T Media Service
Quezon City, 26 August 2025
LA NIÑA WATCH
LOOMING LA NIÑA CONDITIONS
DOST-PAGASA has been continuously monitoring the El Niño Southern Oscillation (ENSO) in the tropical Pacific. ENSO-neutral is most likely to persist until the August-September-October 2025 season. However, model forecasts suggest an increasing probability of short-lived La Niña conditions as early as the September-October-November season until the October-November-December season.  
La Niña (cool phase of ENSO) is characterized by unusually cooler-than-average sea surface temperatures in the central and eastern equatorial Pacific.  When conditions are favorable for the development of La Niña within the next six months and the probability is 55% or more, a La Niña Watch is issued.  
Historically, La Niña is characterized by an above-average number of tropical cyclone occurrences towards the end of the year and above-normal rainfall conditions in most parts of the country that can trigger adverse impacts, including floods and landslides in vulnerable areas. 
DOST-PAGASA will continue to closely monitor the possibility of La Niña conditions and its effect on the local climate. All concerned agencies and the public are encouraged to continue monitoring and take precautionary measures against their potential impacts. 
For more information, please call the Climate Monitoring and Prediction Section (CLIMPS), Climatology and Agrometeorology Division (CAD) at telephone number (02) 8284-0800 local 4920 and 4921 or through email: pagasa.climps@gmail.com.

PRESS STATEMENT
DOST-PAGASA S & T Media Service
Quezon City, 26 August 2025
LA NIÑA WATCH
LOOMING LA NIÑA CONDITIONS
DOST-PAGASA has been continuously monitoring the El Niño Southern Oscillation (ENSO) in the tropical Pacific. ENSO-neutral is most likely to persist until the August-September-October 2025 season. However, model forecasts suggest an increasing probability of short-lived La Niña conditions as early as the September-October-November season until the October-November-December season.  
La Niña (cool phase of ENSO) is characterized by unusually cooler-than-average sea surface temperatures in the central and eastern equatorial Pacific.  When conditions are favorable for the development of La Niña within the next six months and the probability is 55% or more, a La Niña Watch is issued.  
Historically, La Niña is characterized by an above-average number of tropical cyclone occurrences towards the end of the year and above-normal rainfall conditions in most parts of the country that can trigger adverse impacts, including floods and landslides in vulnerable areas. 
DOST-PAGASA will continue to closely monitor the possibility of La Niña, and its effect on the local climate. All concerned agencies and the public are encouraged to continue monitoring and take precautionary measures against their potential impacts. 
For more information, please call the Climate Monitoring and Prediction Section (CLIMPS), Climatology and Agrometeorology Division (CAD) at telephone number (02) 8284-0800 local 4920 and 4921 or through email: pagasa.climps@gmail.com.

𝐈𝐂𝐘𝐌𝐈: Equipping Communities with GeoRiskPH: Two-Day Training in Sogod, Southern Leyte
The two-day GeoRiskPH Training, held in partnership with the Municipality of Sogod, Southern Leyte, successfully brought together thirty-eight participants from the Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Offices, Planning and Development Offices, Engineering Office, Environment and Natural Resources Office, Planning and Development Coordinator, Philippine National Police, and Bureau of Fire Protection.
Throughout the sessions, participants were equipped with knowledge on the different applications offered by the GeoRiskPH Initiative, including the GeoMapperPH mobile and web application, HazardHunterPH and its Pro version, and GeoAnalyticsPH and its Pro version. At the end of the training, a Re-Entry Action Plan Activity was conducted where representatives from various offices shared how they intend to adopt these applications in their respective workflows. Mr. Renan P. Grullo from the Bureau of Fire Protection expressed their interest in using GeoMapperPH for Fire Safety Inspections, while Ms. Sheryl Lura from the Rural Health Unit of Sogod presented initiatives to improve health service delivery, emergency preparedness, and program planning by incorporating geospatial data and tools. These include mapping health facilities, overlaying population data on hazard layers using GeoMapperPH, and utilizing HazardHunterPH for health emergency planning.
In his closing remarks, Vice Mayor Atty. Jose Ramil G. Golo expressed his gratitude to the participants and facilitators and his appreciation for this kind of initiative. He shared his hope that the applications would be integrated into the workflows of local government units, helping them equip themselves to build a safer and more resilient community.

BREAKING: STRONG EARTHQUAKE HITS THE GULF OF ALASKA 
A magnitude 5.1 earthquake struck near Simeonof Island, Gulf of Alaska today, Tuesday, August 26, 2025, at 08:03 UTC.
 Depth: 33 km — shallow enough to be strongly felt in surrounding areas.
 While no tsunami warnings or major damage have been reported so far, the quake’s shallow depth may have amplified shaking along nearby islands and coastal zones. Residents from Kodiak to the Alaska Peninsula have reported tremors.
 This region sits on the volatile Pacific Ring of Fire, one of the most seismically active zones on the planet, where powerful earthquakes and tsunamis have struck in the past.
 Authorities are urging residents to remain alert for aftershocks and to review emergency plans. Earthquakes in this region can occur with little to no warning.
 Stay safe. Stay informed.

A magnitude 5.5 earthquake struck the Caspian Sea late tonight (11:33 PM local time), about 82 km off Dagestan’s coast.
 Shallow depth = more intense shaking, felt widely across southern Russia, Azerbaijan, Georgia, and Armenia.
 This is one of the strongest offshore quakes in the Caspian Sea in recent years, raising concerns about aftershocks in the volatile region.
 Seismologists are closely monitoring the area, as this sector lies near complex fault systems that have produced destructive quakes in the past.
 Residents are urged to stay alert for aftershocks and follow local emergency advisories.

DOST-PHIVOLCS holds a seminar-workshop for 3R (Risk Reduction and Resilience) Tsunami Ready Philippines: Tsunami Ready Community for Cluster 1 - Provinces of Ilocos Sur and Ilocos Norte on August 27-29, 2025 at Fiesta Garden Hotel, Bantay, Ilocos Sur.
Gathering various agencies in the region including the Civil Defense Ilocos Region, DILG Ilocos Region, and DOST 1 - Department of Science and Technology Regional Office No. 1 as well as the Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Offices (DRRMOs) within coastal areas of Ilocos Norte and Ilocos Sur, the 3-day seminar-workshop aims to equip participants on disaster preparedness and response particularly on the threats of tsunami.
Mr. Rhon Arquelada, Provincial DRRMO head of Ilocos Sur representing Governor Jeremias C. Singson of Ilocos Sur Province, sent his opening remarks to the participants of the event. Meanwhile, Dr. Ma. Mylene M. Villegas, Deputy Director of DOST-PHIVOLCS, delivered a message and introduction to Disaster Resilience and Risk Reduction and PHIVOLCS Disaster Mitigation Programs for Tsunami.
Participants were immersed in a series of lectures and workshops from DOST-PHIVOLCS experts. Ms. Joan C. Salcedo, Supervising Science Research Specialist (SRS), led a lecture on Tsunami overview and its impacts. Further, Ms. Fatima M. Moncada, SRS II, shared the Information Tools developed by DOST-PHIVOLCS like HazardHunterPH and REDAS (TsuSIM) which come in handy in times of disasters like tsunami. 
Lastly,  Ms. Charmaine V. Villamil, Senior SRS, discussed the measures of disaster preparedness such as Natural Signs, Philippine Tsunami Information, Safety Preparedness Measures, Structural and Non-structural Mitigation Measure, CBEWS Overview, and IOC/UNESCO Tsunami Ready Recognition Program. She also taught the participants basic map reading.
Participants will continue to learn practical skills in tsunami preparedness in the coming days of the lecture-workshop for them to create action plans in their communities and become ready and resilient against tsunami.
